text:
alice: FYI I ran a focused profiling pass on continuous batching accounting after yesterday's allocator tweak. Found an unusual padding growth pattern when seq lengths cluster around 128-160 tokens. attaching quick notes + flamegraph: https://gist.github.com/rdw/xyz123 :eyes:

ben: nice — what metric flagged it? memory fragmentation or pad amplification?

alice: pad amplification. aggregate per-batch padding went from ~9% to ~18% for a subset of traces. overall GPU util didn't drop but tail OOMs increased on smaller-slabs machines.

carol: do you have per-seq overhead numbers? could be kernel-switch alignment or KV cache tagging causing extra workspace per item.

alice: per-seq overhead (measured by instrumenting workspace alloc): baseline ~540 bytes/seq, spike up to ~820 bytes/seq for those clustered buckets. meaning for batches of 64 that’s an extra ~18MB workspace.

dan: that maps to the pad buckets being rounded to 192 by our pad-slope heuristic? we added a conservative ceil in last deploy.

alice: yeah looks like the heuristic is bumping to next power-of-two-ish step. here's the snippet I used to simulate:```python
# simulate pad growth
seqs = [128]*30 + [150]*34
pad = [ceil_to_slope(s) for s in seqs]
sum(pad)-sum(seqs)
```

ben: interesting — so continuous batching growth + slope rounding = compounding padding. Did you check KV cache hits? maybe cache entries force longer kv prefixes.

alice: perf traces show KV cache hit-rate stable, but KV shadowing causes some requests to carry extra KV metadata (~64 bytes/seq) when fallback kernels are selected.

carol: any correlation with kernel selection logs? eg kernel-fallback -> workspace-reserve larger.

alice: yes. when the kernel selector switches to the fallback attention kernel (for seqs > 140 with certain optimizations disabled), it requests a larger workspace alignment. I captured the kernel log lines:```json
{"ts":1958004325,"kernel":"attn_fallback","workspace_req":3145728}
{"ts":1958004326,"kernel":"attn_opt","workspace_req":2097152}
```

dan: so two levers: pad-slope granularity and kernel workspace alignment. For OOM mitigation we could a) tighten slope ceil thresholds b) let allocator suballocate across sequences to reuse leftover workspace c) prefer kernel that uses split-kv allocation.

ben: a) easy short-term. drop slope steps when mean(seq) < 160. b) requires allocator change — we can try soft-sharing a workspace per-batch rather than per-seq and track per-seq offsets. risk: increased synchronization.

carol: do we have perf numbers for soft-sharing? I remember an experiment where soft-sharing reduced pad waste by ~40% but added 1.8ms median latency for small batches.

alice: I reran a microbench: soft-sharing prototype reduced pad amplification from 18% -> 7% on the burst traces, and OOMs vanished on 24GB cards. Median latency +0.9ms, P99 +3.2ms for 8-16 token tails. Tradeoff looks acceptable for Dedicated tier but maybe not Hosted default.

perf-bot: [perf-regression-check] baseline_vs_prototype: median_lat:+0.9ms, p99_lat:+3.2ms, pad_waste:-61%, memory_peak:-22% :white_check_mark:

dan: sounds promising. propose we land slope tweak as quick fix for Hosted and schedule allocator soft-sharing POC behind a runtime flag for Dedicated. Also add kernel selector telemetry so we can PID matching traces to kernel choices.

alice: agreed. I'll open two PRs: 1) slope tweak + unit tests 2) soft-sharing flag + microbench harness. also will add a perf metric dashboard tile for kernel-selector proportions and pad amplification per-model.

ben: can you include a regression guard so we don't accidentally bump latency for PLG churn? maybe gate on customer_tier != hosted for the soft-sharing flag.

alice: yup will gate it. ETA for PRs: slope tweak today, soft-sharing draft by EOD tomorrow.

carol: awesome. also let's add a quick on-call note in incidents if we see OOM surge after slope change, so SRE can rollback.

alice: added to my checklist. thanks all :thumbsup:
